segments.title: Post-nine-eleven security expansion
segments.narration: Anti-terrorism statutes, no-fly logic, and expanded intelligence powers arrive with continental pressure. Oversight and transparency do not expand at the same speed. The pattern: capability first, accountability later — if at all.

segments.title: Sponsorship scandal — modern patronage on camera
segments.narration: The Auditor General and Gomery inquiry expose advertising kickback networks after the referendum. Public trust in federal Liberals collapses. The scandal is a teaching case in procurement, parties, and the difference between audit findings and criminal closure.

segments.title: Harper years — control, energy, and centralization of message
segments.narration: Minority then majority Conservative government emphasizes fiscal messaging, resource development, and tight communications control. Accountability office fights and data controversies enter the public record. The film neither hagiographs nor demonizes — it tracks statutes, budgets, and audits.

segments.title: Apology, TRC, and the unfinished implementation
segments.narration: The residential school apology and TRC process produce Calls to Action. Implementation scorecards later show uneven progress. The film treats promises as measurable claims against open trackers.

segments.title: Phoenix pay — the seed of a nine-billion failure
segments.narration: A payroll transformation for the public service is planned under one government and detonates under the next. The Auditor General will later document a multi-billion remediation. Phoenix is the archetype of digital state failure that prefigures ArriveCAN-scale scandals.

segments.title: Century Initiative and demographic planning assumptions
segments.narration: A one-hundred-million population aspiration enters elite planning discourse. Immigration targets rise. Housing supply, healthcare capacity, and infrastructure lag. The film will later place targets against CMHC and Health Canada numbers — not slogans.

segments.title: After September 11 — security state expansion
segments.narration: Anti-terrorism statutes, no-fly lists, and intelligence budgets expand after two thousand one. Oversight lags. The security state and the welfare state reverse trajectories — more surveillance capacity, thinner social capacity. Primary statutes and SIRC/NSICOP reports are the evidence.

segments.title: Sponsorship Scandal and Gomery
segments.narration: The Sponsorship Scandal and Gomery Inquiry document Liberal Party of Canada era misuse of public funds for political ends. It is a textbook case of patronage networks. The public accounts and inquiry transcripts remain online.

segments.title: Harper years — census, omnibus, Afghanistan
segments.narration: Long-form census cancellation fights, omnibus bills, Afghanistan combat, and accountability office creation coexist. The film does not romanticize any party. It tracks instruments of power: how statutes, budgets, and appointments move regardless of brand colour.
